clue.text: Movement of troops? Record is linked to sudden movements

parts.note: a log is a written record, as in a ship's log
taken as written
tics are sudden involuntary twitches

explanation.surface: A military historian notes that a diary entry ties troop moves to sudden twitches.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition is a loose description: the business of moving and supplying troops.
explanation.definitionFit: The planning and transport of military forces and their supplies is what this word first meant.

clue.text: Rude words, except about learner's facial care

parts.note: lip is cheeky, insolent talk

indicators.note: about means the word for except goes round the learner's letter

parts.note: save can mean except, as in 'all save one'
L is the learner sign on British cars

explanation.surface: Someone avoids rude language except when discussing a student's skincare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts L inside SAVE, making SALVE.
explanation.definitionFit: A balm smeared on the mouth to soothe chapped skin is a piece of facial care.

clue.text: Italian port's good — excellent in retrospect

indicators.note: looking back in time suggests reading the word for excellent backwards

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, spelt here as A ONE

explanation.surface: A travel review praises an Italian harbour town, looking back on a fine visit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in retrospect' turns A ONE into ENOA.
explanation.definitionFit: The city is a major seaport on the Ligurian coast of north-west Italy.

clue.text: Intoxicated around pass, drunken Boers? By no means

indicators.note: around means the word for intoxicated wraps the mountain pass

parts.note: stoned is slang for high or drunk
a col is a pass between mountain peaks

indicators.note: drunken signals that the letters of Boers stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: Drunken Afrikaners staggering round a mountain pass, the setter insists, are anything but sober.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Intoxicated' does double duty in the surface: the definition 'By no means' answers it, meaning not intoxicated at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Completely clear-headed is the opposite of drunk, so this is what someone is when they are not intoxicated in the slightest.

clue.text: Leaflets in papers? Very popular, sure things, we hear

parts.note: in means fashionable, popular

indicators.note: we hear means the next word is to be judged by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: certs is British slang for certainties, usually racing tips

explanation.surface: A newspaper claims its free flyers are both popular and guaranteed winners.
explanation.walkthrough: CERTS (slang for certainties, from horse racing) is said like SERTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose advertising sheets tucked into newspapers and magazines are called by this name.

clue.text: Dog, quick on the uptake, that is leaping up

parts.note: sharp means mentally quick

indicators.note: in a down clue, leaping up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A clever dog is jumping up at its owner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaping up' turns IE into EI.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrinkled Chinese breed is named this, so it is a kind of hound.

clue.text: Scoundrel curtailed swindle

indicators.note: curtailed means a tail cut off, so the last letter of the word for scoundrel is dropped

parts.note: a scamp is a rascal or rogue

explanation.surface: A rogue's fraud is cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: A fraudulent scheme to cheat people is a con of this kind.

clue.text: Drink making you race in and out drunkenly

indicators.note: drunkenly means the letters lurch about into a new order

explanation.surface: A barman warns that this liqueur sends you reeling in and out of the room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunkenly' rearranges RACE IN and OUT.
explanation.definitionFit: A French orange-flavoured liqueur is a drink.

clue.text: Being silent about it is this?

definitions.text: Being silent about it is this?

indicators.note: about means the word for silence wraps round the contracted 'it is'

parts.note: mum means saying nothing, as in 'keep mum'
'tis is the poetic contraction of it is

explanation.surface: A riddle asks what we call the state of saying nothing about something.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines the answer: the condition of refusing to speak is literally a state of keeping mum about 'tis.
explanation.definitionFit: Refusing or being unable to speak is the medical condition of muteness.

clue.text: Urgent letters suggesting good protection for battle

definitions.text: Urgent letters suggesting good protection for battle

parts.words: Urgent letters suggesting good protection for battle
parts.note: the priority postal service also reads as top-quality chain armour worn in combat

explanation.surface: A soldier writes home urgently asking for better armour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mail' is both post and armour of linked metal rings; the prompt postal service reads as top-grade armour.
explanation.definitionFit: The faster priority postal service carries urgent letters.

clue.text: Long opening in original Christmas show

parts.note: to pant for something is to long for it

indicators.note: opening in points to the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A long-running festive show opens with something original.
explanation.walkthrough: PANTO is a British Christmas stage show for families, with slapstick and audience participation.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for pantomime, the comic family play staged in Britain over the festive season.

clue.text: Taint surrounding Left -it's disturbed left-winger

indicators.note: surrounding means the word for taint wraps the letter for left

parts.note: a stain is a taint or blemish

indicators.note: disturbed means the letters of it's are stirred up

explanation.surface: A slur clings to the left, and a troubled radical results.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surrounding' puts L in STAIN to make STALIN; 'disturbed' turns IT'S into IST.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of the Soviet dictator's hardline communism is a hard leftist.

clue.text: Gold Rush initially snared friend, one not normally interested in money

definitions.text: one not normally interested in money

indicators.note: snared means the gold symbol traps the word for friend inside it

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
mate is British for friend

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of Rush

explanation.surface: In a gold rush, a prospector catches a pal who doesn't care about wealth.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes someone who does something for love rather than pay; 'Gold Rush' is a false phrase pulling toward prospecting.
explanation.definitionFit: A non-professional who takes part without payment is not in it for money.

clue.text: Money some in Europe set aside

indicators.note: some in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some cash in Europe has been put by.
explanation.walkthrough: The run spans 'EuroPE SET ASide'; these were the Spanish coins before the euro set them aside.
explanation.definitionFit: The former Spanish currency units are a form of cash.

clue.text: Unpleasant group of people that becomes progressively worse

explanation.surface: A nasty clique's situation keeps deteriorating.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally the phrase is a nasty set of people; as an idiom it is a chain of cause and effect that keeps worsening.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally a nasty clique; as an idiom, a situation where each problem feeds the next so matters keep deteriorating.

clue.text: Jewel of a part? Hardly

parts.note: a carved gem gives its name to a small showy acting appearance, which is barely a part at all

explanation.surface: A critic asks whether a tiny role was a gem, and decides it barely counts.
explanation.walkthrough: A cameo is a carved jewel and also a brief film appearance, which is hardly a part.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief appearance by a well-known actor in a film or play is barely a part.

clue.text: Dress in feathers to eradicate resistance?

parts.note: to wear clothes is to be dressed in them
down is the soft fine feathering of birds

explanation.surface: Someone dons a feather costume to break down opposition.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the definition stretches: gradually overcoming opposition until none is left.
explanation.definitionFit: To erode someone's opposition by persistence until they give in.

clue.text: Particularly fitting, as a ruler is?

explanation.surface: A tailor says a suit fits perfectly, like a measuring stick.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is literal: a ruler is manufactured in order to measure.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothes tailored to one person fit especially well; and a ruler is literally produced for gauging length.

clue.text: What some lace-makers do, left out of gossip

indicators.note: out of means the letter for left is removed from the word for gossip

parts.note: tattling is idle gossiping

explanation.surface: Some lace-makers are left out of the chatter.
explanation.definitionFit: Making knotted lace with a shuttle by hand is a craft some lace-makers practise.

clue.text: Man leading navy around very good source of water

indicators.note: leading means the word for man comes before the abbreviation for navy
around means the joined letters wrap the abbreviation for very

parts.note: male means a man
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: A sailor leads the fleet round a fine spring.
explanation.walkthrough: MALVERN, in the English hills of that name, is famous for its bottled spring water.
explanation.definitionFit: The English spa town gives its name to a well-known bottled mineral water.

clue.text: Dance observed to be a puzzle

parts.note: a jig is a lively folk dance
saw is the past tense of see, observed

explanation.surface: Someone watching a dance finds it baffling.
explanation.definitionFit: A picture cut into interlocking pieces to be reassembled is a kind of brain-teaser.

clue.text: Make clear indication of golfer's readiness?

explanation.surface: A golfer takes out a club, ready to sort things out.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is literal: a golf club called an iron, out of the bag and ready to play.
explanation.definitionFit: To smooth away problems, as with creases; and literally a golfing club drawn from the bag.

clue.text: More forceful one involved in unexpected result…

indicators.note: involved in means the numeral is placed inside the rearranged letters
unexpected means the letters of result are jumbled

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A single figure is mixed up in a surprise outcome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unexpected' rearranges RESULT, and 'involved in' places I among those letters to give LUSTIER. The ellipsis leads on to the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Comparative of vigorous: having more strength and energy.

clue.text: I had to surmount island's way of speaking

indicators.note: in a down clue, to surmount means to sit on top of, so the first piece comes above the second

parts.note: I'd is the contraction of I had
IOM is the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: A traveller had to conquer an island's dialect.
explanation.walkthrough: IOM is the Isle of Man, an island in the Irish Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: An expression whose meaning is peculiar to a language is part of its manner of talking.

clue.text: … result? Twenty nil, reversed before end of game

indicators.note: before places the reversed word ahead of the final letter

parts.note: a score is twenty

indicators.note: reversed means the word for nothing is read backwards

parts.note: nil means nothing

indicators.note: end of points to the last letter of game

explanation.surface: A match ends twenty-nil, with the score turned round late in the game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversed' turns NIL into LIN. The ellipsis joins this to the previous clue's 'result'.
explanation.definitionFit: The final score of a match is its outcome.

clue.text: Am I to leave friend from overseas?

parts.note: taken as written
to go is to leave

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether they should depart from a foreign companion.
explanation.walkthrough: AMIGO is Spanish for friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Spanish word for a pal, used in English for a mate.

clue.text: Architect's emotional stress, eliminating church

indicators.note: eliminating means the abbreviation for church is removed

parts.note: a wrench is a painful emotional parting

explanation.surface: An architect suffers heartache but drops his church project.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Christopher WREN designed St Paul's Cathedral in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Christopher of that name was the English designer of St Paul's Cathedral.

clue.text: Chap's information to identify officer recalled

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

indicators.note: recalled means the words for identify and officer are read backwards as one run

parts.note: to name someone is to identify them
Lt is short for lieutenant

explanation.surface: A man's information helps identify an officer who was called back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' turns NAME + LT into TLEMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A man, especially a courteous one, is a fellow.
